nightdash-bot: ALERT: nightly-perf: 95p latency +32% vs 7d baseline on route=kernel-selection. metric=latency_95p, scope=production-nightly, dashboard=https://internal.redwood/perf/nightdash/206420
maya: saw the alert, digging into the spike graph now
maya: baseline shows a step up at 02:12 UTC, coincides with last deploy
aleks: i merged a small prober ordering tweak in #3345 yesterday afternoon, could be related
jon: pinging CI perf job to compare before/after: `perf-ci compare --metric latency_95p --range 2064100000..2064200000`
ci-bot: perf-ci started, comparing commits 0a1b2c3 -> f9e8d7c (PR #3345)
ci-bot: result: latency_95p increased 28% on kernel-selection path, p95 tail widened. throughput unchanged.
maya: logs from a select machine show increased KV evictions during long sequences:
```
[2026-03-17T02:12:34Z] kv_evictions/sec: 410
[2026-03-17T02:12:34Z] kv_cache_size_mb: 512 -> 320
[2026-03-17T02:12:34Z] kernel_prober: preferred_order=[stream,kernel_v2,kernel_v1]
```
aleks: i only changed `kernel_prober` ordering to prefer stream-first to reduce cold start latency for short chats. didn't touch kv settings
sam: that reordering can change kernel handoff frequency, could cause more kv cache thrash if stream mode flushes early
jon: running a targeted bisect across the merge window now, starting with the PR bump and related infra commits
nate: any chance batching window changes rolled in too? did the merge include `batcher/default_window_ms` tweak?
maya: i grepped release diff: #3345 touched runtime/prober and a yaml tweak in infra/configs/batcher.yaml (default_window_ms: 8 -> 12)
jon: aha. bigger batching window + stream-first prober could interact: longer windows mean more overlapping KV lifetimes but stream preference can cause more frequent kernel switches
ci-bot: bisect finished: commit f9e8d7c (PR #3345) is the first bad commit for latency_95p on kernel-selection route
aleks: rolling back the prober reorder in a hotfix branch now
sam: can we do a canary rollback on dedicated pool A only? avoid global revert if possible
maya: agree — hold release and gate rollout. I'll open a canary revert and run nightly perf again
maya: creating revert PR #3351 reverting prober ordering and batcher tweak
maya: PR #3351 created: https://git.internal/rdw/infra/pulls/3351
jon: kicking off canary deploy to pool-a
ci-bot: deploy started to pool-a (canary) @ 2064200600
jon: monitoring KV eviction rate and latency after canary
ci-bot: interim metrics (pool-a): kv_evictions/sec -> 95, latency_95p -> baseline +-3%
nate: can confirm pool-a looks back to normal
aleks: bad interaction — my change was intended to help short chats but I missed wider perf interaction with batching defaults
maya: follow-ups: 1) add unit/integration test that simulates prober handoffs under heavy KV load, 2) add perf guardrail to CI that runs a lightweight tail-latency check on kernel-selection paths when prober ordering or batcher defaults change, 3) investigate adaptive batch-window that respects kernel handoff stability
sam: i'll file an infra ticket for the CI guardrail
sam: TKT-1427 created: CI perf guard for kernel-selection changes
maya: leaving the global rollback on hold; we'll merge the revert after canary confirms across two more pools
aleks: sorry about the churn, will add better perf notes to PRs
nate: small note for postmortem: label any prober/batcher changes as HIGH-RISK for nightly tail-latency dashboards
maya: i'll ping customers impacted by nightly anomaly if we see any related error ramp; unlikely but prepared
jon: closing loop: canary looks good, merge revert PR scheduled after 30m stable window. tracking on the release board.
nightdash-bot: ALERT CLEARED: nightly-perf: latency_95p back within baseline after canary revert (clear at 2064201200) :white_check_mark:
